title: Sorting, Filtering & Dynamic Arrays · Excel Lesson 6 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Organise data with single and multi-level sorts and custom orders, find what matters with AutoFilter and Advanced Filter, and then let formulas do it for you with the dynamic array functions UNIQUE, SORT, SORTBY, FILTER and SEQUENCE, plus the power tool SUMPRODUCT.

title: Lookup Functions: VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP and INDEX-MATCH · Excel Lesson 7 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Bring data together from different tables. Master VLOOKUP and HLOOKUP (exact and approximate match), the modern XLOOKUP, the flexible INDEX + MATCH combination (including two-way and reverse lookups), OFFSET, consolidating several sheets, CHOOSE, and how to troubleshoot

title: Pivot Tables from Basic to Advanced · Excel Lesson 8 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Summarise thousands of rows in seconds. Build pivot tables, understand the pivot cache and the four areas, change value field settings, show values as % of total, MoM and YoY change and running totals, group dates and numbers into bins, add calculated fields, slicers and timelines, and solve the Video Game Sales case study.

title: Date, Time & Number Functions and Named Ranges · Excel Lesson 9 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Work confidently with dates and times (DATE, EOMONTH, EDATE, WORKDAY, NETWORKDAYS, WEEKDAY, WEEKNUM, DATEDIF, fiscal quarters), clean up numbers with INT, MOD, ROUND, CEILING and FLOOR, and make formulas readable with static and dynamic named ranges and LET.

title: Charts and Advanced Charts · Excel Lesson 10 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Choose the right chart for every question, build and format column, bar, line, area, pie, scatter and combo charts, add sparklines, and create the advanced business charts taught in class: thermometer, Pareto, population pyramid and waterfall, plus histogram, box plot, treemap and funnel.

title: Interactive Dashboard: Superstore Case Study · Excel Lesson 11 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Build a complete, interactive sales dashboard from the Superstore data, from business questions and KPIs to pivot charts, slicers, a timeline, KPI cards and a dynamic title. Then protect it (sheet, workbook, allowed ranges), document it with comments and notes, and audit formulas with Evaluate Formula.

title: Power Query, Power Pivot, Analysis ToolPak & What-If Analysis · Excel Lesson 12 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Automate cleaning with Power Query (import, transform, unpivot, merge, append, group), model several tables with Power Pivot and DAX, get descriptive statistics and regression from the Analysis ToolPak, plan with Goal Seek, Data Tables, Scenario Manager and Solver, and meet LAMBDA, Python in Excel and macros.

title: Flash Fill, Text to Columns and Standardising Messy Data · Excel Lesson 13 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Clean messy exports fast. Use Flash Fill to learn a pattern from examples, Text to Columns to split values, and formulas to standardise case, spacing, phone numbers and dates, then check every result before you rely on it.

title: Excel Macros and VBA: Recording and Writing Automation · Excel Lesson 14 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Automate a repeated monthly report. Record a macro, read the code it writes, change it to work on any data, add a loop over several sheets, and keep macro files safe from untrusted code.

title: Office Scripts, Power Automate and AI-Assisted Excel Formulas · Excel Lesson 15 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Automate Excel on the web with Office Scripts written in TypeScript, run them on a schedule with Power Automate, and use AI assistants to draft formulas, with a checklist for testing every formula before you rely on it.

title: Excel Business Projects: Complaints, Finance, Productivity and Segmentation · Excel Lesson 16 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Four portfolio-ready Excel projects, each from a business brief. Analyse customer complaints, build a financial performance tracker, measure employee productivity, and segment customers with a sales performance dashboard, using the skills from the course.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) Complete Guide: The Role, Skills, AI Deployments, Integrations and Interviews · FDE Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Understand the Forward Deployed Engineer role made famous by Palantir and now central at AI companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic and at enterprise software firms. Learn what FDEs do, the skills stack (software engineering, data, AI/LLM systems, integrations, cloud, security, customer skills), the deployment lifecycle from discovery to production, how to build and evaluate LLM solutions for customers, integration patterns, a capstone deployment and how to prepare for FDE interviews.

title: How Large Language Models Work: Tokens, Embeddings, Transformers and Training · GenAI & Agents Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Open the black box. Tokens and tokenisation (built from scratch), next-token prediction and sampling with temperature, embeddings, attention and the transformer, pre-training, instruction tuning and RLHF, context windows, reasoning models, why LLMs hallucinate, and how to choose among Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek and Qwen.

title: Prompt Engineering in Depth: Patterns, Templates, Few-Shot, Reasoning and Structured Output · GenAI & Agents Lesson 2 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Write prompts that work reliably in products, not just in chat. The anatomy of a production prompt (role, context, task, constraints, format, examples), XML tags and delimiters, few-shot examples chosen by similarity, step-by-step reasoning and extended thinking, structured JSON output with validation, prompt templates and versioning, prompt chaining, and a simple evaluation loop.

title: Calling LLM APIs from Python: Messages, Streaming, Structured Output, Costs and Reliability · GenAI & Agents Lesson 3 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Move from the chat window to code. Set up API keys safely, send messages with system prompts, hold multi-turn conversations, stream responses, get schema-valid JSON, control reasoning effort, cache long prompts, count tokens and estimate cost, batch large jobs, handle errors and retries, and run the same pattern with other providers, with a runnable offline simulator for practice.

title: Embeddings and Vector Search: Meaning as Numbers, Similarity and Vector Databases · GenAI & Agents Lesson 4 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn the foundation of semantic search and RAG. What embeddings are, how word and sentence embeddings are learned (trained here from scratch on our reviews), cosine similarity, document embeddings, building a vector index, exact vs approximate nearest-neighbour search (IVF, HNSW), evaluating retrieval with recall@k, hybrid keyword + vector search, and choosing embedding models and vector databases.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Build, Evaluate and Improve a Q&A Assistant · GenAI & Agents Lesson 5 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Ground an LLM in your own documents. RAG architecture, document loading and chunking, indexing, hybrid retrieval and re-ranking, prompt assembly with citations, answer generation (offline simulator plus real Claude code with the citations feature), evaluation of retrieval and answers, failure modes and advanced patterns (query rewriting, contextual retrieval, metadata filters, agentic and graph RAG), built end to end on a retailer's policy handbook.

title: Tool Use and Function Calling: Letting LLMs Query Data, Call APIs and Take Actions · GenAI & Agents Lesson 6 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Connect a model to the outside world. How function calling works (tool definitions, JSON schemas, tool_use and tool_result blocks), the request–execute–respond loop, writing good tool descriptions, strict schemas and validation, parallel calls, error handling, server-side tools (web search, code execution), and safety controls, with a runnable sales-analytics assistant that answers questions by calling SQL and calculator tools.

title: AI Agents and Agentic AI: Loops, Planning, Memory, Multi-Agent Systems and When to Use Them · GenAI & Agents Lesson 7 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Understand what makes software "agentic". Workflows vs agents, the agent loop (observe, think, act), ReAct-style reasoning with tools, planning and task decomposition, short- and long-term memory, guardrails and stopping conditions, multi-agent patterns (orchestrator–workers, evaluator–optimiser, routing), the 2026 agent platforms, and how to decide whether a problem needs an agent at all, with a runnable data-analysis agent.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): Connecting AI Assistants to Your Data and Tools · GenAI & Agents Lesson 8 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn the open standard that lets any AI application use any tool or data source. MCP architecture (hosts, clients, servers), the three primitives (tools, resources, prompts), transports (stdio and Streamable HTTP), building and testing a real MCP server for sales data in Python, connecting it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code and other clients, using remote MCP servers from the API, and securing MCP deployments.

title: Evaluating LLM Applications and Building Guardrails: Test Sets, LLM-as-Judge, Injection, PII and Safety · GenAI & Agents Lesson 9 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Ship GenAI features you can trust. Build evaluation sets, choose metrics (exact match, rubric scores, groundedness), calibrate LLM-as-judge against humans, run regression tests on every prompt change, and protect applications with input and output guardrails: prompt-injection defences, PII detection and redaction (Indian identifiers), schema validation, refusal handling, red-teaming and production monitoring.

title: Customising Models: Prompting vs RAG vs Fine-Tuning, LoRA, Distillation and Open-Weight Models · GenAI & Agents Lesson 10 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Decide how to adapt a model to your task. The customisation ladder (prompting, few-shot, RAG, tools, fine-tuning, training), what fine-tuning is good and bad at, preparing training data, parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA and QLoRA (with the maths), distillation from a large to a small model, running open-weight models locally with Ollama and at scale with vLLM, and the cost, privacy and quality trade-offs of API vs self-hosting.

title: GenAI for Data Work: Text-to-SQL, AI Coding Assistants, Data Cleaning and Automated Insights · GenAI & Agents Lesson 11 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Apply LLMs to everyday analytics and engineering. Schema-aware text-to-SQL with guardrails and execution-accuracy evaluation, AI coding assistants and agents in notebooks and IDEs, LLM-assisted data cleaning (normalising messy categories, extracting fields from text), generating narrative insights from tables safely, and a workflow that keeps the analyst in control.

title: Building and Shipping a GenAI App: Architecture, Streamlit/FastAPI, Cost, Observability and Responsible AI (Capstone) · GenAI & Agents Lesson 12 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Put the GenAI track together. Reference architecture for an LLM application, a support-assistant capstone (RAG + tools + guardrails + evaluation), a Streamlit chat front end and a FastAPI back end, session memory, streaming, cost and latency budgets, caching, observability and tracing, deployment options, a launch checklist and responsible-AI governance, with a runnable cost and capacity planner.

title: Business Problem-Solving: KPIs, Process Mapping, Discovery and Hypotheses · Governance Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Turn a vague business complaint into a measurable problem. Define KPIs and the drivers beneath them, map a process to find its bottleneck, run stakeholder discovery with Five Whys and a fishbone diagram, and write testable hypotheses and recommendations with an owner and a measure.

title: Requirements, User Stories, PRDs, Data Storytelling and Agile Delivery for Analytics · Governance Lesson 2 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Specify analytics work so that it gets built right the first time. Write requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria, draft a product requirements document, communicate findings with data storytelling, and run analytics delivery in short agile cycles with a backlog, sprints and reviews.

title: Data Ownership, Stewardship, Retention and Privacy Law: GDPR and India's DPDP Act · Governance Lesson 3 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Assign clear ownership and stewardship to each dataset, set and enforce retention periods, and apply the core principles of privacy law, including data minimisation, consent and purpose, individual rights and breach reporting under the EU's GDPR and India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

title: Data Masking, Row-Level Security and Access Control · Governance Lesson 4 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Protect sensitive data while keeping it useful. Mask values in queries and in views, show only the last digits of identifiers, restrict which rows each user sees with row-level security, and audit who accessed what, with worked examples in SQL and Python and a regional report protected through RLS.

title: Responsible AI, Threat Modelling and Incident Response · Governance Lesson 5 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Build AI systems that are fair, transparent, overseen and secure. Check model performance across groups, threat-model the data, prompts, tools and outputs of an AI application, and plan detection, containment, repair and communication for an incident, with a worked example of a prompt-injection leak.

title: Digital Marketing Complete Guide: Strategy, SEO, Google and Meta Ads, Social, Email, WhatsApp, Analytics and AI · Marketing Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: A complete digital marketing guide for India. Build a strategy and funnel, research customers and keywords, do on-page, technical and local SEO plus AI search (AEO/GEO), run Google Ads and Meta Ads with the right bidding, targeting and creatives, grow social and influencer programmes, run email and WhatsApp marketing, measure with GA4, UTMs and attribution, optimise conversion rates, plan budgets with unit economics, and use AI tools responsibly, with a full campaign capstone.

title: Descriptive Statistics: Centre, Spread, Shape and Relationships · Stats & ML Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Describe data with numbers before modelling it. Types of data and measurement scales, mean, median and mode, range, variance, standard deviation, IQR and coefficient of variation, percentiles and z-scores, skewness and kurtosis, covariance and correlation (Pearson and Spearman), all on the house-price and HR datasets.

title: Probability and Distributions: Rules, Bayes, Binomial, Poisson and Normal · Stats & ML Lesson 2 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: The language of uncertainty. Probability rules, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem (with a fraud-alert example), random variables and expected value, and the distributions analysts use most (Bernoulli, binomial, Poisson, uniform, normal, exponential), with scipy.stats and simulation.

title: Sampling, the Central Limit Theorem and Confidence Intervals · Stats & ML Lesson 3 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn how a sample tells us about a population. Population vs sample, sampling methods and biases, sampling distributions and standard error, the Central Limit Theorem by simulation, confidence intervals for means and proportions (z, t and bootstrap), and how to choose a sample size.

title: Hypothesis Testing I: The Framework, p-values, z-tests and t-tests · Stats & ML Lesson 4 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Turn business questions into testable hypotheses. Null and alternative hypotheses, significance level, test statistics, p-values and critical values, one- vs two-tailed tests, Type I and II errors and power, then one-sample, two-sample (Welch) and paired t-tests and z-tests for proportions, on a delivery-time case study.

title: Hypothesis Testing II: Chi-Square, ANOVA, Non-Parametric Tests and Correlation Tests · Stats & ML Lesson 5 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Test relationships between categories with chi-square tests, compare three or more groups with one-way ANOVA and Tukey post-hoc tests, use non-parametric alternatives (Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis) when assumptions fail, test correlations, and control false discoveries when running many tests.

title: A/B Testing and Experimentation: Design, Power, Analysis and Pitfalls · Stats & ML Lesson 6 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Run product experiments the way data teams at e-commerce and fintech companies do. Choose a metric and guardrails, size the test with power analysis, randomise, analyse conversion and revenue with z-tests, t-tests and bootstrap intervals, check sample-ratio mismatch, avoid peeking and novelty effects, and write the decision memo, using a new-checkout experiment.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning: Types, Business Framing and the ML Lifecycle · Stats & ML Lesson 7 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: What machine learning is and is not, how it differs from rules and statistics, supervised vs unsupervised vs reinforcement learning, regression vs classification vs clustering, turning a business problem into an ML problem, the end-to-end ML lifecycle (CRISP-DM to MLOps), linear vs non-linear models and link functions, and where GenAI fits.

title: The scikit-learn Workflow: Train/Test Split, Baselines, Pipelines and Saving Models · Stats & ML Lesson 8 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn the standard machine-learning workflow in scikit-learn. The estimator API (fit, predict, transform), splitting data into train, validation and test sets with stratification and time order, baselines, ColumnTransformer and Pipeline to avoid leakage, comparing models, and saving and loading a trained pipeline.

title: Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering for ML · Stats & ML Lesson 9 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Prepare features that models can learn from. Imputation strategies, outlier handling, encoding categorical variables (one-hot, ordinal, target encoding), scaling (standard, min-max, robust), transformations (log, Box-Cox/Yeo-Johnson), binning, interactions and polynomial features, date and text features, and feature selection, all inside leak-free pipelines.

title: Linear Regression: Fitting, Interpreting, Assumptions and Diagnostics · Stats & ML Lesson 10 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Predict a number and explain it. Simple and multiple linear regression with ordinary least squares, interpreting coefficients, dummy variables and log targets, R², adjusted R², RMSE and MAE, the LINE assumptions and residual diagnostics, multicollinearity and VIF, outliers and influence, with statsmodels for inference and scikit-learn for prediction on the house-price data.

title: Gradient Descent: How Models Learn (Built from Scratch in NumPy) · Stats & ML Lesson 11 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Understand the optimisation engine behind linear regression, logistic regression and neural networks. Cost functions, gradients and the update rule, implementing batch gradient descent for linear regression in NumPy, the learning rate, feature scaling, stochastic and mini-batch variants, convergence checks, and comparison with the closed-form OLS solution and scikit-learn's SGDRegressor.

title: Overfitting, Polynomial Regression and Regularisation (Ridge, Lasso, Elastic Net) · Stats & ML Lesson 12 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: See overfitting and underfitting happen, learn the bias-variance trade-off with polynomial regression, and control model complexity with L2 (Ridge), L1 (Lasso) and Elastic Net penalties, including choosing the penalty strength with cross-validation, feature selection with Lasso, and learning curves.

title: Logistic Regression: Probabilities, Odds Ratios and Credit-Risk Scoring · Stats & ML Lesson 13 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Classify with probabilities. The sigmoid and log-odds, maximum likelihood and log loss, fitting logistic regression with statsmodels (inference, odds ratios) and scikit-learn (pipelines, regularisation), thresholds and decisions, multiclass logistic regression, and scoring new applicants in the Bank Loans case study.

title: Classification Metrics: Confusion Matrix, Precision, Recall, ROC, PR and Business Value · Stats & ML Lesson 14 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Measure classifiers properly. The confusion matrix, accuracy and why it misleads, precision, recall, specificity, F1 and F-beta, ROC curves and AUC, precision-recall curves, log loss and calibration, lift and gains charts, choosing thresholds by cost or capacity, and multiclass averaging, using the telecom churn model.

title: Cross-Validation and Hyperparameter Tuning: K-Fold, GridSearchCV, RandomizedSearchCV and Optuna · Stats & ML Lesson 15 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Estimate performance reliably and tune models without fooling yourself. Hold-out vs k-fold, stratified, grouped and time-series cross-validation, cross_validate with several metrics, GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV over pipelines, nested cross-validation, Bayesian optimisation with Optuna, and the common leakage traps.

title: K-Nearest Neighbours: Classifier and Regressor (Bank Loans Case Study) · Stats & ML Lesson 16 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: The simplest learning algorithm: predict from the most similar past examples. Distance metrics, choosing k, why scaling is essential, weighted voting, the curse of dimensionality, KNN for classification and regression, tuning with GridSearchCV, and the full Bank Loans case study from the live class with metrics and scoring of new applicants.

title: Decision Trees: Splits, Impurity, Pruning and Interpretable Rules · Stats & ML Lesson 17 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn the model behind random forests and gradient boosting. How trees split data with Gini impurity, entropy and variance reduction, growing and visualising a tree, reading it as business rules, controlling overfitting with depth, minimum leaf size and cost-complexity pruning, regression trees, feature importance and the strengths and weaknesses of single trees.

title: Ensembles I: Bagging and Random Forests · Stats & ML Lesson 18 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Combine many models to beat one. The wisdom of crowds, bootstrap aggregating (bagging), random forests with feature subsampling, out-of-bag evaluation, the key hyperparameters, feature importance (impurity vs permutation), extra trees, voting and stacking ensembles, applied to telecom churn.

title: Ensembles II: Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost · Stats & ML Lesson 19 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: The algorithm family that wins most tabular-data problems. Boosting intuition (AdaBoost to gradient boosting), fitting trees to residuals by hand, learning rate and number of trees, early stopping, scikit-learn's HistGradientBoosting, XGBoost and LightGBM APIs and key hyperparameters, categorical features and CatBoost, and a tuned comparison on churn and house prices.

title: Support Vector Machines and Naive Bayes · Stats & ML Lesson 20 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Two classic classifiers with very different ideas. SVMs find the widest margin between classes, use soft margins (C) and kernels (RBF, polynomial) for non-linear boundaries, and need scaling; Naive Bayes applies Bayes' theorem with an independence assumption and is a fast, strong baseline for text. Includes SVR, probability calibration and when to choose each.

title: Imbalanced Classification: Fraud Detection with Class Weights, Resampling and Thresholds · Stats & ML Lesson 21 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Most valuable classification problems are rare-event problems (fraud, defaults, churn, failures). Learn why accuracy and naive training fail, the right metrics (PR-AUC, recall at fixed precision, cost), class weights, undersampling, oversampling and SMOTE inside pipelines, threshold moving, and anomaly-detection alternatives, on a synthetic card-fraud dataset with about 1.4% fraud.

title: Clustering I: K-Means and RFM Customer Segmentation · Stats & ML Lesson 22 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Find groups without labels. Heuristic RFM segmentation (recency, frequency, monetary scores and named segments) as taught in class, then K-means clustering, scaling and log transforms, choosing k with the elbow method and silhouette score, profiling and naming clusters, and turning segments into marketing actions, on 4,500 retail transactions.

title: Clustering II and Dimensionality Reduction: Hierarchical, DBSCAN, Gaussian Mixtures, PCA, t-SNE and UMAP · Stats & ML Lesson 23 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Go beyond K-means. Agglomerative hierarchical clustering with dendrograms and linkage choices, density-based DBSCAN for irregular shapes and outliers, Gaussian mixture models with soft assignments, and dimensionality reduction with PCA (explained variance, loadings, compression), plus t-SNE and UMAP for visualisation, applied to video-game sales and HR data.

title: Time-Series Forecasting: Decomposition, Baselines, ETS, ARIMA and ML with Lag Features · Stats & ML Lesson 24 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Forecast demand properly. Components of a time series (trend, seasonality, noise), decomposition with STL, stationarity and autocorrelation (ADF, ACF/PACF), honest baselines (naive, seasonal naive, moving average), exponential smoothing (Holt-Winters), SARIMA, machine learning with lag and calendar features, backtesting with forecast metrics (MAE, RMSE, MAPE, WAPE), prediction intervals, and a guide to Prophet, statsforecast and foundation models.

title: NLP and Text Analytics: Cleaning, TF-IDF, Sentiment Classification, Topics and Embeddings · Stats & ML Lesson 25 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Turn customer reviews into insight. Text cleaning and tokenisation, stop words, stemming and lemmatisation, bag-of-words and TF-IDF with n-grams, a sentiment classifier with error analysis, aspect-level insight, topic modelling with NMF, document similarity, and how embeddings and LLMs change NLP, on 3,000 e-commerce reviews.

title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning: From a Neuron to Transformers · Stats & ML Lesson 26 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Understand the models behind modern AI. Neurons, weights and activation functions, forward pass and backpropagation, a two-layer network written from scratch in NumPy, multilayer perceptrons in scikit-learn on images and tabular data, training practice (learning rate, batches, epochs, early stopping, dropout), and a map of CNNs, RNNs, transformers and LLMs with PyTorch and Keras code.

title: Explainable AI and MLOps: SHAP, Fairness, Deployment, Monitoring and Responsible ML · Stats & ML Lesson 27 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Make models trustworthy and useful in production. Global and local explanations (permutation importance, partial dependence, SHAP), fairness checks across groups, packaging a pipeline, serving predictions with FastAPI, batch scoring, experiment tracking with MLflow, monitoring data drift and performance, model cards, and the regulations and responsible-AI practices that apply in India and globally.

title: ML Capstone: End-to-End Churn Prediction and Retention Strategy · Stats & ML Lesson 28 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Put the whole ML track together. Frame the churn problem, build leak-free features, compare baselines and models with cross-validation, tune the winner, choose a profit-maximising threshold under a budget, explain predictions, design segment-level retention actions with an A/B test, and write the model card, deployment plan and executive summary for your portfolio.

title: Recommendation Systems: Collaborative, Content-Based and Hybrid · Stats & ML Lesson 29 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Build recommenders that suggest the next product or item. Learn collaborative filtering from a user-item matrix, content-based filtering from item features, how to combine them, how to handle new users, and how to evaluate with precision at k and hit rate without recommending what people already own.

title: Regression Metrics: MAE, MSE, RMSE and R-Squared · Stats & ML Lesson 30 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Measure how wrong a numeric prediction is, in the units the business uses. Compute MAE, MSE, RMSE and R-squared on a delivery-time model, learn which metric punishes big mistakes, see why R-squared alone misleads, and explain each metric to a manager.

title: Getting Started with Power BI & Your First HR Report · Power BI Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Understand what Power BI is and how its parts fit together, install Power BI Desktop, tour the three views, follow the ETL and analytics stages, and build a complete first report on HR data: cards, bar and column charts, a donut, slicers, a year column with DAX, groups and small multiples.

title: Power Query, Star Schema & Data Modelling (Adventure Cycles) · Power BI Lesson 2 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Prepare and model data the professional way. Clean data in Power Query, load a star schema (fact and dimension tables), create one-to-many relationships, understand filter direction, build and mark a date table, create hierarchies, and avoid the most common modelling mistakes, using the Adventure Cycles case study.

title: DAX Fundamentals: Measures, Filter Context & CALCULATE · Power BI Lesson 3 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn DAX, the formula language of Power BI. Understand calculated columns vs measures, row context vs filter context, write core aggregations and iterators (SUMX), master CALCULATE and FILTER, ALL/REMOVEFILTERS and ALLSELECTED, handle division safely, use variables, and build a library of business measures.

title: DAX Time Intelligence, Ranking, Parameters & Dynamic Measures · Power BI Lesson 4 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Make dashboards answer "compared with when?". Build year-to-date, month-to-date, same-period-last-year, month-on-month and year-on-year measures, rolling averages, rankings with RANKX and TOPN, what-if parameters, field parameters and dynamic measure switching, and know visual calculations and calculation groups.

title: Visuals, Filters, Drill-through, Tooltips, Buttons & Report Design · Power BI Lesson 5 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Turn a model into an interactive, well-designed report. Choose visuals, format them (cards, matrix, charts, gauge, KPI, maps, images), use visual, page and report filters, edit interactions, drill-down and drill-through, custom tooltips, bookmarks and buttons, conditional formatting, themes and design principles.

title: Power BI Service, Connectivity Modes, Security & Capstone · Power BI Lesson 6 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Take a report from Desktop to the people who need it. Understand Import, DirectQuery, Live connection, composite models and Direct Lake, publish to the Service, schedule refresh with a gateway, share through workspaces and apps, secure data with row-level security, tune performance, work with Copilot and Fabric, and complete the Adventure Cycles capstone.

title: Microsoft Fabric: Lakehouse, Warehouse, Dataflows and Semantic Models · Power BI Lesson 7 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Understand Microsoft Fabric as one platform. Load data into a lakehouse, shape it in a warehouse or dataflow, publish a semantic model that Power BI reports read from, and keep the whole chain governed and refreshed.

title: Databricks: Notebooks, Delta Lake, Spark Jobs and Unity Catalog · Power BI Lesson 8 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Work on a lakehouse with Databricks. Write notebooks in SQL and PySpark, store tables as Delta Lake with merges and time travel, run Spark jobs on a schedule, and govern data with Unity Catalog so that reports read trusted tables.

title: Introduction to Python: Why, Install & Jupyter Notebooks · Python Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn what programming and Python are, how Python compares with other languages, how code runs (interpreters, compilers, bytecode), the properties of Python, and set up your environment (Anaconda, VS Code, Jupyter, Google Colab). Write and run your first cells, with markdown, magic commands and good notebook habits.

title: Variables, Data Types, Type Conversion, print(), f-strings & input() · Python Lesson 2 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Store and name values with variables, meet Python's core data types (int, float, str, bool, None, complex), convert between types, format output with print(), f-strings and .format(), and read user input with input() and sys.argv.

title: Operators, Strings, Indexing, Slicing & String Methods · Python Lesson 3 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Master Python's operators (arithmetic, comparison, logical, assignment, membership, identity, bitwise) and work with text: string indexing and slicing, immutability, every string method an analyst needs (split, join, strip, replace, find, startswith, case methods, isdigit…), escape sequences, and cleaning real messy text.

title: Control Flow: if, elif, else, Nested Conditions & match · Python Lesson 4 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Make programs decide. Learn indentation, if/elif/else, comparison and logical conditions, truthiness, conditional expressions (ternary), nested decisions, the match statement, and how Python's if maps to Excel's IF/IFS and SQL's CASE WHEN, with data-flavoured examples.

title: Loops: while, for, range, break, continue & Patterns · Python Lesson 5 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Repeat work without repeating code. Learn while and for loops, range(), enumerate(), zip(), break, continue, the loop else clause, nested loops, accumulation, search and counting patterns, and common loop bugs; with an eye on when to replace loops with vectorised pandas/NumPy.

title: Lists: Creating, Slicing, Methods, Sorting & Comprehensions · Python Lesson 6 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Store and process ordered collections with lists. Index and slice them, add, remove and sort items, understand mutability, aliasing and copying (shallow vs deep), use nested lists, list comprehensions, and common patterns for cleaning and summarising data.

title: Tuples & Sets: Immutable Records, Unpacking and Set Algebra · Python Lesson 7 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Use tuples for fixed records and multiple return values, master unpacking and named tuples, and use sets for uniqueness, fast membership tests and set algebra (union, intersection, difference) on real customer data.

title: Dictionaries: Key-Value Data, Counting and Grouping · Python Lesson 8 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Store and look up data by key. Create and update dictionaries, use get, setdefault, items, Counter and defaultdict, nest dictionaries, and convert between dictionaries, JSON-like records and DataFrames using the Superstore data.

title: Functions: Reusable Code, Arguments, Scope and Docstrings · Python Lesson 9 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Package logic into reusable functions. Learn def, parameters and arguments (positional, keyword, default, *args, **kwargs), return values, scope, docstrings and type hints, plus testing small functions on real data.

title: Comprehensions, Lambda, map/filter and Generators · Python Lesson 10 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Write compact, readable Python. Learn list, set and dict comprehensions, lambda with sorted/min/max, map and filter, any and all, generators and itertools, and when plain loops or pandas are the better choice.

title: Object-Oriented Python: Classes, Objects, Inheritance and Dataclasses · Python Lesson 11 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Model real things as objects. Learn classes, __init__, attributes and methods, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, special (dunder) methods, class and static methods, properties and dataclasses, with a small data-pipeline example.

title: Files, Exceptions, JSON and CSV · Python Lesson 12 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Read and write text, CSV and JSON files safely with pathlib and with-blocks, handle errors with try/except/else/finally, raise your own exceptions, and log what happened, using a small "load a messy file" project.

title: Modules, Packages, Virtual Environments and Git · Python Lesson 13 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Organise code into modules and packages, install libraries with pip or uv inside virtual environments, pin dependencies, use the standard library, and version-control your projects with Git and GitHub.

title: Debugging, Testing, Regular Expressions and Code Quality · Python Lesson 14 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Find and fix bugs systematically, write automated tests with pytest, clean text with regular expressions, and keep code readable with PEP 8, type hints, linters and formatters.

title: NumPy: Fast Arrays, Vectorisation and Broadcasting · Python Lesson 15 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn the array library under pandas, scikit-learn and PyTorch. Create arrays, understand shape and dtype, index and slice in 1-D and 2-D, filter with boolean masks, compute with vectorised operations, aggregations along axes and broadcasting, generate random data and do basic linear algebra.

title: pandas I: Series, DataFrames, Reading Data, Selecting and Filtering · Python Lesson 16 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Meet the most-used data library. Create Series and DataFrames, read CSV and Excel files, inspect data with head, info and describe, select columns and rows with loc and iloc, filter with conditions and query, sort, add columns and save results, using the Superstore sales data.

title: pandas II: Data Cleaning: Missing Values, Types, Duplicates, Text and Outliers · Python Lesson 17 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Turn messy data into analysis-ready data. Detect and treat missing values, fix data types, remove duplicates, standardise text, parse dates, handle outliers with IQR and caps, and document every step in a reusable cleaning function.

title: pandas III: GroupBy, Pivot Tables, Merge/Join and Reshape (melt/unpivot) · Python Lesson 18 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Summarise and combine data. Use groupby with agg, transform and filter, build pivot tables and crosstabs, join tables with merge (inner, left, right, outer, anti), stack with concat, and reshape between wide and long with melt, pivot, stack and unstack.

title: pandas IV: Dates, Time Series, Resampling and Rolling Windows · Python Lesson 19 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Work with time. Parse dates, extract parts with .dt, do date arithmetic, set a DatetimeIndex, resample to weeks, months and quarters, compute rolling and expanding windows, shifts and growth rates, and build a cohort-style monthly report with the daily sales data.

title: Data Visualisation I: Matplotlib and Choosing the Right Chart · Python Lesson 20 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Pick the right chart for the question and build it with Matplotlib's object-oriented API. Line, bar, histogram, scatter, box and pie charts, subplots, annotations, styling and saving, plus design rules that make charts honest and readable.

title: Data Visualisation II: Seaborn Statistical Charts and Interactive Plotly · Python Lesson 21 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Make statistical charts quickly with Seaborn (distributions, categorical comparisons, relationships, correlation heatmaps, pair plots and facets) using the HR attrition data, and build interactive charts and simple dashboards with Plotly Express and Streamlit.

title: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) Case Study: Telecom Customer Churn · Python Lesson 22 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Run a complete, structured EDA on 3,000 telecom customers. Frame the question, check data quality, do univariate, bivariate and segment analysis, engineer features, quantify revenue at risk and finish with findings and recommendations: the template you will reuse for every dataset and for the ML churn model.

title: Python and SQL: sqlite3, DuckDB, SQLAlchemy and pandas.read_sql · Python Lesson 23 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Connect Python to databases. Create and query SQLite with the standard library, use parameterised queries safely, load DataFrames to tables and back, query CSV and DataFrames directly with DuckDB, connect to MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server with SQLAlchemy, and decide what to do in SQL versus pandas.

title: APIs, JSON and Web Scraping with requests and BeautifulSoup · Python Lesson 24 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Collect data from the web. Understand HTTP, call REST APIs with requests (GET/POST, query parameters, headers, authentication, pagination, retries and rate limits), flatten nested JSON with json_normalize, and scrape HTML tables and pages responsibly with BeautifulSoup and pandas.read_html.

title: Performance and Bigger Data: Vectorisation, Memory, Parquet, Polars and DuckDB · Python Lesson 25 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Make Python data work fast and scale beyond memory. Measure with timeit, replace loops with vectorised code, shrink DataFrames with the right dtypes, store data as Parquet, use Polars lazy queries and DuckDB for out-of-core analytics, and know when to move to Spark and the cloud.

title: DSA I: Big-O, Arrays, Strings, Hashing, Two Pointers and Sliding Window · Python Lesson 26 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Data structures and algorithms for data-analyst, data-scientist and data-engineer interviews. Learn Big-O time and space complexity, then the patterns that solve most array and string questions (hash maps and sets, prefix sums, two pointers, sliding window), with worked interview problems and timings.

title: DSA II: Stacks, Queues, Linked Lists, Recursion, Sorting and Binary Search · Python Lesson 27 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn linear data structures (stack, queue, deque, linked list), recursion and backtracking, the main sorting algorithms with their trade-offs, and binary search including "search on the answer", with interview problems such as valid parentheses, next greater element, reverse a linked list and search in a rotated array.

title: DSA III: Trees, Heaps, Graphs (BFS/DFS) and Dynamic Programming · Python Lesson 28 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Finish the DSA toolkit. Binary trees and binary search trees with traversals, heaps and priority queues with heapq (top-k, merge k lists, running median), graphs with adjacency lists, BFS and DFS, shortest paths and topological sort (as used in data pipelines), and dynamic programming from memoisation to tables.

title: Python Capstone: End-to-End Retail Sales Analytics Project · Python Lesson 29 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Bring the whole Python track together on the Superstore data. Structure a project, build a validated data pipeline, compute KPIs, growth and Pareto analysis, cohort retention and discount impact, create a chart pack and an Excel report, and write the README and executive summary you can put in your portfolio.

title: Automation: Scheduled Scripts, Reports and Email · Python Lesson 30 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Turn a manual report into a script that runs on a schedule, reads the data, builds a summary, logs every run and sends the result by email without storing a password in the code.

title: Production Python: Logging, Type Hints, Packaging and Code Organisation · Python Lesson 31 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Make Python code that other people can run, read and trust. Structure a project into modules, add type hints and check them with mypy, log what a pipeline does without leaking secrets, and package the code so it installs with one command.

title: Salesforce Marketing Cloud (SFMC) Complete Guide: Email Studio, Data Extensions, SQL, AMPscript, Journey Builder and Certification · SFMC Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: A complete training guide to Salesforce Marketing Cloud Engagement for marketers, analysts and developers. Learn the architecture and studios, subscribers and data extensions, data modelling and Contact Builder, SQL Query Activities, segmentation, Content Builder and AMPscript personalisation, Email Studio sends, Automation Studio, Journey Builder, Mobile Studio (SMS, push, WhatsApp), deliverability, consent and the DPDP Act, reporting, Einstein AI, Data Cloud and Agentforce, plus a capstone and the Marketing Cloud Email Specialist and Administrator certification paths.

title: Public Speaking Complete Guide: Confidence, Structure, Storytelling, Delivery, Slides, Meetings, Interviews and Video · Speaking Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: A practical guide to speaking with confidence at work and on stage. Manage nerves, structure any talk with proven frameworks, tell stories with data, design clear slides, master voice, pace and body language, handle Q&A and tough questions, speak in meetings, interviews and stand-ups, present on video and in hybrid rooms, and practise with AI tools, with a 30-day plan and a capstone talk.

title: Databases, RDBMS & SQL Basics · SQL Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Understand what a database is, how relational databases organise data into tables, the vocabulary of SQL, the four families of SQL statements (DDL, DML, DCL, TCL), how SQL compares with Excel, and how to install SQL Server and SSMS and run your first query.

title: ER Diagrams, Relationships, Keys & Normalisation · SQL Lesson 2 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Design databases the way professionals do. Draw ER diagrams, read crow's-foot notation, model one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many relationships, master every type of key (super, candidate, primary, alternate, composite, foreign, surrogate) and normalise tables to 3NF.

title: Data Types, Operators, NULLs, Variables & Comments · SQL Lesson 3 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Choose the right SQL Server data type for every column, use arithmetic, comparison, logical and string operators correctly, understand NULL and three-valued logic, declare variables, follow naming rules and write readable, commented SQL.

title: DDL, DML & Constraints: CREATE, ALTER, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE · SQL Lesson 4 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Create and change tables with DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE), add, change and remove rows with DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE), protect data quality with constraints (PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK, DEFAULT, IDENTITY) and understand DELETE vs TRUNCATE vs DROP.

title: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY & Filtering Operators · SQL Lesson 5 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Retrieve exactly the rows and columns you need. Master SELECT, aliases with AS, DISTINCT, TOP, WHERE with comparison and logical operators, IN, BETWEEN, LIKE wildcards, IS NULL, ORDER BY, and the logical order in which SQL processes a query.

title: SQL Functions: Aggregate, Text, Date & Number · SQL Lesson 6 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Use SQL Server's built-in functions to summarise, clean and reshape data. Aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, STRING_AGG), text functions (LEN, LEFT, RIGHT, SUBSTRING, CHARINDEX, REPLACE, TRIM, UPPER, CONCAT), date functions (GETDATE, YEAR, MONTH, DATEPART, DATENAME, DATEADD, DATEDIFF, EOMONTH) and number functions (ROUND, CEILING, FLOOR, ABS, POWER, SQRT), plus CAST and CONVERT.

title: GROUP BY, HAVING, CASE WHEN, ROLLUP, CUBE & COALESCE · SQL Lesson 7 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Turn rows into business summaries. Group with GROUP BY, filter groups with HAVING, create conditional columns and buckets with CASE WHEN, pivot data with conditional aggregation, and add subtotals and grand totals with ROLLUP, CUBE and GROUPING SETS, cleaning the labels with COALESCE and GROUPING().

title: Joins and a Retail Case Study · SQL Lesson 8 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Combine tables with INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER, CROSS and SELF joins, find missing matches with anti-joins, avoid the classic join mistakes (row explosion, filters in ON vs WHERE), and answer a full set of business questions on the retail database.

title: Set Operators: UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT & EXCEPT · SQL Lesson 9 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Stack and compare query results. Append data with UNION ALL, remove duplicates with UNION, find common rows with INTERSECT and differences with EXCEPT, follow the rules for compatible columns, and know when to use a set operator instead of a join.

title: Subqueries, Derived Tables & EXISTS · SQL Lesson 10 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Put queries inside queries. Use scalar subqueries, multi-row subqueries with IN, ANY and ALL, correlated subqueries, EXISTS and NOT EXISTS, and derived tables (inline views) to answer questions that one level of SELECT cannot, and learn when a join, CTE or window function is better.

title: OFFSET-FETCH and Window Functions I: OVER, PARTITION BY & Ranking · SQL Lesson 11 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Page through results with OFFSET and FETCH, then learn window functions, the most powerful analytics feature in SQL. Understand OVER and PARTITION BY, rank rows with ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK and NTILE, solve top-N-per-group and de-duplication problems, and compare aggregate windows with GROUP BY.

title: Window Functions II: Running Totals, LEAD, LAG & Frames · SQL Lesson 12 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Build time-series analytics in SQL. Use window frames (ROWS BETWEEN) for running totals and moving averages, LAG and LEAD for month-on-month and year-on-year growth, FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE, cumulative percentages, PERCENT_RANK, CUME_DIST and PERCENTILE_CONT, and gaps-and-islands patterns.

title: CTEs, Views, Temporary Tables, Stored Procedures & Functions · SQL Lesson 13 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Write queries other people can read and reuse. Use CTEs (including recursive CTEs for hierarchies and calendars), create views for reusable logic and security, use temp tables and table variables, and build stored procedures, user-defined functions, parameters and basic error handling in T-SQL.

title: Transactions, Indexes, Performance & Security · SQL Lesson 14 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Make SQL safe and fast. Understand transactions and ACID (BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVE), isolation and locking, indexes (clustered, non-clustered, covering), how to read an execution plan, a checklist for writing fast queries, and permissions with GRANT, REVOKE and roles (DCL).

title: End-to-End SQL Case Study & Interview Practice · SQL Lesson 15 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Put everything together. Work through a complete analysis of the retail business (data quality, KPIs, trends, customer segmentation, retention, product and discount analysis) using joins, CTEs and window functions, then practise 25 classic SQL interview questions with model answers.

title: Recursive CTEs, Hierarchies and Number Series · SQL Lesson 16 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Use recursive common table expressions to walk hierarchies such as org charts and category trees, build number and date series without a calendar table, and avoid runaway recursion.

title: Percentiles, Medians and Distribution Queries · SQL Lesson 17 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Go beyond averages. Compute medians and percentiles, split customers into quartiles and deciles, measure how skewed a distribution is, and find outliers with SQL that works on real retail data.

title: Business SQL: Cohorts, Funnels, Churn, Lifetime Value and Retention · SQL Lesson 18 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Write the SQL behind the business questions that analysts are asked every week: cohort retention, conversion funnels, churn, customer lifetime value and retention rates, using the retail database.

title: Incremental Loading and Data-Quality SQL · SQL Lesson 19 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Load only what has changed, using watermarks, MERGE and upserts, and protect the warehouse with reusable data-quality checks for nulls, duplicates, orphans, ranges and freshness.

title: SQL Across Platforms: SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake and Databricks SQL · SQL Lesson 20 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn the same analysis on the four platforms most job postings name, see where their SQL dialects differ (dates, string functions, limits, top-N, identifiers), and know which platform concept maps to which.

title: Getting Started with Tableau: Interface, Data Connections and Your First Views · Tableau Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Understand the Tableau product family, install Tableau Public, connect to the Superstore India data, read the Data Source page, learn dimensions vs measures and discrete vs continuous fields, master the Marks card and shelves, build and sort your first views, and save them to Tableau Public.

title: Charts in Tableau: From Bar and Line to Maps, Dual Axis, Histograms and Pareto · Tableau Lesson 2 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Build every core chart in Tableau and know when to use each: bar, stacked and side-by-side bars, line and area, pie and donut, treemap, highlight table, scatter plot, histogram with bins, box plot, filled and symbol maps, dual-axis combo charts, bullet charts and a Pareto chart, all on the Superstore India data.

title: Calculations in Tableau: Calculated Fields, Table Calculations and LOD Expressions · Tableau Lesson 3 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Write calculated fields (row-level and aggregate), use string, date, number and logical functions, handle nulls, then master table calculations (running total, percent of total, difference and growth, rank, moving average, and Compute Using) and Level of Detail expressions (FIXED, INCLUDE, EXCLUDE), with every result checked against pandas.

title: Filters, Parameters, Sets, Groups and Hierarchies in Tableau · Tableau Lesson 4 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Control what a view shows and let users interact with it. Learn every filter type and where it sits in the order of operations, context filters and Top N, groups, hierarchies, bins, sets (fixed, conditional, top) and combined sets, and parameters for dynamic Top N, measure swapping and what-if analysis.

title: Data Modelling in Tableau: Relationships, Joins, Unions, Blending, Extracts and Tableau Prep · Tableau Lesson 5 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Combine and shape data in Tableau. Understand the logical layer (relationships) and the physical layer (joins), when to union or blend, how row duplication inflates totals, live connections vs extracts, data interpreter and pivoting, and how Tableau Prep Builder cleans data in repeatable flows, using the Adventure Cycles star schema.

title: Dashboards, Actions, Stories and Publishing in Tableau (Capstone) · Tableau Lesson 6 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Turn sheets into an interactive dashboard and a data story. Plan the layout with containers, add filter, highlight, URL, parameter and set actions, design for phones, tell a story with Story Points, publish to Tableau Public or Cloud, and complete two capstones, a Superstore India sales dashboard and the video-game regional sales case study from class.

title: Figma Complete Tutorial: Interface, Auto Layout, Components, Variables, Prototypes, Dev Mode and Figma AI · Tools Lesson 1 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn Figma from zero to a handoff-ready design. Tour the interface, master frames, shapes, text and the 8-point grid, build responsive layouts with auto layout and constraints, create components with variants and properties, use styles and variables (light and dark modes), prototype flows with Smart Animate and overlays, hand off in Dev Mode, run workshops in FigJam, and generate working prototypes with Figma AI and Figma Make. Includes a dashboard-design project for data roles.

title: n8n Complete Tutorial: Workflow Automation, Data Pipelines and AI Agents · Tools Lesson 2 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Learn n8n, the open, self-hostable workflow-automation tool. Set it up on n8n Cloud or Docker, understand triggers, nodes, credentials, items and expressions, transform data with Edit Fields, IF, Switch, Merge, Loop and Code nodes, call any API with HTTP Request, handle errors and schedules, build AI agents with chat models, memory, tools and vector stores, and connect n8n to MCP. Four complete projects: lead capture, a daily sales report, an email-triage AI agent and a document Q&A bot.

title: Tools and Learning Resources Directory: How to Choose and Evaluate Tools · Tools Lesson 3 · Data Science & AI Handbook
desc: Use a structured directory of tools across sixteen categories, from spreadsheets and SQL to MCP and portfolio tools, and evaluate any AI or no-code tool with a repeatable sheet covering purpose, features, limits, strengths, weaknesses and alternatives.
